label: 03 · Packaged ports
description: All 26 workflows as *.quiet-choir packages: the six Batch 02 rewrites, and the other twenty ported straight from Batch 01 with fixture modules of their own. Prose is in typed markdown templates, rosters use std fragments and tiers, panels and the review loop come from std patterns, three packages compose others as children, and a decider screens the SDLC stage reviews.
validation: Root-strict TypeScript; CLI validation of every package with no prompt warnings; the Batch 02 fixture intents with real temporary Git and test commands, actual SIGKILL recovery and the F1–F5 matrix; every agent call rendered from a template; requireGrants delegation; and CLI fixture decisions for autoApprove. 70 recorded results, no live agents or decision host: they measure orchestration contracts, not model quality.
commonChanges: Each workflow is a <name>.quiet-choir package (ADR 0065): package.ts names the entry, workflows/ holds control flow only, contracts.ts the Zod schemas, roster.ts the agents, prompts.ts and prompts/ the prose, lib/ the mechanics and, for test-gap-filler, resources/ its mutation worker. Every file under the root is fingerprinted, so a template or resource edit is refused on resume like a code edit.

Every agent prompt is a MiniJinja template with typed parameters (ADR 0064), checked before any effect; the verifier asserts that every agent call records its template. With prose out of the control flow, the templates carry the upstream's guidance, much of which Batch 02 had cut to one line.

Rosters spread std.claude and std.codex capability fragments, with std.tiers models on Claude entries, so every role pins a model and effort; the upstream's per-call effort choices return as entries. Roles are narrow: drafters, judges and rankers have no tools, and only the roles that edit files can write.

Code owns the effects the upstream asked agents to perform or report. Commands run through ctx.exec and std.exec, and agents receive their output; artifacts are written by ctx.writeFile with an ifMatch guard, as an exclusive create or a replace of the version code read; and agent writers work in runtime-owned worktrees pinned to a recorded base, where code checks each receipt against the files the writer may change before ctx.merge publishes it.

Fan-outs are settled: a ctx.map with onError: 'return', or std.patterns.tolerantPanel (bug-hunt, dead-code-sweep, flaky-test-hunt), so a failed member is saved as data and stays failed on resume instead of being retried into a different result. release-notes' fact-check loop is std.patterns.reviewRevise.
What a human must approve, a plan to write or probes to run, is a durable approval whose subject carries the exact plan or list and its SHA-256 digest; a declined approval writes or runs nothing.

Three packages compose others as typed inline children: sdlc-orchestrator runs project-bootstrap and release-notes, feature-factory runs prd-decompose and deep-code-review, and prd-to-spec runs design-tournament. Under --require-grants the children delegate onto the parent's roster entries, and sdlc-orchestrator's autoApprove is a Gatekeeper decision-provider screen (ADR 0066) whose fallback is the human review.

Packages import only quiet-choir and its std and decision subpaths, plus the sibling packages they compose, so the small contracts (Sha, Path, Argv) are repeated per package instead of shared through a batch helper. The originals are the same pinned bytes. The six keep Batch 02's interfaces and the twenty the upstream's, except where a note says an input or output was added, dropped or changed; nothing here measures model quality.
apiFindings: A roster cannot be subset: roster: { Reviewer: roster.Reviewer } fails typecheck (TS2353). The package reference no longer shows it, and the SDLC package declares one roster per workflow; #794 tracks spreading a roster.

std.patterns.reviewRevise returned { approved, draft } without the critic's last feedback, so release-notes reports factChecked rather than Batch 02's concern list. It now also returns feedback and the number of reviews, and takes a retry policy; #766 proposes typed drafts and verdicts.

std.patterns.tolerantPanel returned answers without their items, so a failed vote could not be named and several ports fell back to a settled ctx.map. It now returns outcomes, each answer or saved failure with its item and index, and takes key and retry; #753 and #754 propose pairing and per-item seating.

Template whitespace needs care: trimBlocks also eats the newline after an include, so a fragment that is its own paragraph needs {% include … +%} (documented; #765 proposes a warning). A parameter named range was shadowed by MiniJinja's range() in the unused-parameter check; a parameter that shadows a global now counts as read.

std.tiers are Claude-only, so Codex entries set effort on the std.codex fragment directly, and the SDLC delegation ceilings are roster entries the orchestrator itself never calls. A Codex sandbox confines writes and network, not reads.

Settled failures carry too little: a failed file effect settles without a structured reason, a missing file reads as a process failure (#755) and some path failures fail the run instead of settling (#756); a settled command does not tell a command that could not start from one that failed, and keeps too little of its output, truncation and duration (#760–#764).

Worktrees: there is no read-only isolated call, shared pinned checkout, fresh checkout for ctx.exec or launch-time provisioning (#770–#773), a shared handle gives no per-effect receipt (#774), and ctx.merge does not pin the commit it integrates onto (#768). A rename receipt named only its destination; it now names the source as from.
Packages re-implement canonical-JSON digests, bounded approval previews, receipt ownership checks, the Path, Sha and Argv schemas and quote checks (#785–#788), and a clean-checkout preflight (#759).

Porting the twenty produced 37 triaged clusters. 32 were repaired in the runtime, std and docs on this branch, among them grant refusals that list every missing grant, schema failures that name each failing path, a typed CompletedExecResult and record revision 22, and one in the lab's own fixture contract and fault matrix; the 46 issues #753–#798 on #594 record what remains.

apiSnapshot.description: Validated against the quiet-choir API whose model file has this hash, with workflow packages, prompt templates, roster-only roles, std fragments, tiers and patterns, teams and decision providers. This model-file hash is provenance for that file, not the entire runtime; the ports import the built checkout.
